independent_checks.formal_diagonal: Multiplying (1+x)^(-2n) by (1-x)^(-1) exactly converts the coefficient into the partial sum S_n. The standard small-root residue formula with X=z/(1+X)^2 then gives G=(1+X)/((1-X)(1+3X)).
independent_checks.algebraic_equation: Direct substitution z=X(1+X)^2 and G=(1+X)/((1-X)(1+3X)) reduces the displayed cubic equation to zero.
independent_checks.recurrence_extraction: In the differential certificate, the coefficient of z^(n+2) is exactly P0(n)S_n+P1(n)S_(n+1)+P2(n)S_(n+2); the residual 40z has no contribution for n>=0.
independent_checks.ore_factorization: Expanding (-4P0+P2 E)(E-1/4) with coefficients on the left yields P0+(-4P0-P2/4)E+P2E^2, and 16P0+4P1+P2=0 supplies the stated middle coefficient.
independent_checks.boundary_identity: The first-order factor gives u_n=S_(n+1)-S_n/4. Its exact product solution and binom(3n,n+1)=2n*binom(3n,n)/(n+1) give the denominator-free coupling.
independent_checks.item229_rewrite: Substitution of Q(s)t_(s+1)=2s(2s+1)(4S_(s+1)-S_s) into the frozen Item229 formula gives the displayed two-coordinate identity without division.
independent_checks.same_row_lift: For k<p, generalized binomial coefficients give binom(-2s,k)=binom(p-2s,k) mod p; the row relation turns p-2s into 4s+4h+3. The fixed-h generating function follows by the same diagonal lemma.
independent_checks.literature: Reindexing k=n-j gives S_n=(-1)^n A371813(n). The OEIS parametrization transforms by g(-z)=1/(1+X), and its recorded recurrence shifts to the frozen P0/P1/P2 recurrence. No novelty is claimed.
